[Kara+o+ṇaya(ṇi)]  CL=8 Anta: A word form that can express both suddha-rūpa ("do") and kārita-rūpa ("make to do").
For suddha-rūpa:
- Use ṇaya suffix according to 'surāditō ṇē ṇayā' (Kaccāyana"s rule)
- Use ṇi suffix according to 'surāditōṇi' (Moggallāna"s rule)
For kārita-rūpa:
- Kaccāyana"s method: use ṇaya suffix
- Moggallāna"s method: use ṇi suffix
The word 'kāreti' can be used as an example, as it represents both suddha-rūpa and kārita-rūpa.
Meanings:
(a) Doing (suddha-rūpa)
(b) Causing to do (kārita-rūpa)

The letter (sa) is characterized as follows:
- It is the 38th letter among the 41 letters of the Pali alphabet
- It is the 30th among the 33 consonants
- Among the six classes of sounds (kaṇṭhaja, etc.), it belongs to the dental class (dantaja)
- It is a non-grouped letter (avagga) rather than a grouped letter (vagga)
- It is the 5th letter among the 8 ungrouped consonants
- It is unvoiced (aghosa) rather than voiced (ghosa)
- Among the four tongue positions, it belongs to the middle-tongue position (jivhāmajjha)
- Among the four types of articulation (payatta), it belongs to the open articulation (vivaṭa payatta)
- Between the two types of consonants (those depending on preceding vowels and those depending on following vowels), it belongs to the parāsaya class (depending on following vowels)

The letter "s" is of three kinds -- (1) ekakkhara sa. (2) anekakkharasuddha sa which is merely "s" which is not mixed with other consonants. (3) saṃyogavanta "s" - conjunct "s" which exists together with seven consonants: t, n, m, y, r, v and s. The story of Saṅkicca Sāmaṇera:
Having accumulated merit under previous Buddhas and developed strong conditions for Nibbāna across many lives, he took rebirth in a wealthy brahmin family in Sāvatthī during our Buddha"s time. His mother died during pregnancy due to illness. When her body was being cremated, the womb remained unburned. People pierced it with bamboo stakes and covered it with embers. Though the womb burned, the golden-colored infant remained alive, as if sleeping on a lotus.
For one in their final birth (pacchimabhavika-satta), even Mount Meru cannot prevent them from attaining Arahantship - death cannot occur before this achievement. The next day, people finding the sleeping infant were amazed that he survived while his mother"s body burned completely. They took him to the village and consulted fortune-tellers.
The fortune-tellers predicted: 'If this child remains a householder, his relatives will suffer poverty for seven generations. If he becomes a monk, he will travel with 500 monk followers.' He was named 'Saṅkicca' because his eye was pierced by a bamboo stake (saṅkunā chinnakkhikoṭitāya Saṅkicco - Thera.Ṭṭha.2.213). This name became well-known. His relatives decided that despite the prediction of poverty, they would have him ordained under Venerable Sāriputta when he grew up..
